tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Making Economic Choices

questions.question: Explain how scarcity affects consumers, producers, and government differently.
questions.correctAnswer: Scarcity affects all agents: consumers have limited income; producers have limited resources; government has limited tax revenue. All face opportunity costs and must prioritise.

questions.question: Describe how a consumer might weigh costs and benefits when deciding to buy a £500 laptop.
questions.correctAnswer: Costs: £500 reduces savings, less for other purchases. Benefits: enables study, access to resources, earning potential. The consumer weighs: will the laptop's benefits exceed its opportunity cost (what the £500 could earn in savings, or other goods)? If needed for a course leading to a career, long-term benefit likely exceeds cost.

questions.question: Evaluate whether government spending on defence or healthcare creates greater benefit.
questions.correctAnswer: Defence benefits: security, deterrence, employment. Healthcare benefits: healthier population, longer lives, productive workforce, reduced inequality. Both are essential, but healthcare directly improves more lives per pound in peacetime. The optimal balance depends on the threat environment.

questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: quantify costs (tuition £9,250/yr, living costs, 3 years lost earnings ~£60k opportunity cost); quantify benefits (graduates earn ~£10k/yr more, lower unemployment); consider uncertainty (not all degrees lead to high earnings); conclude: university is rational for most if the wage premium exceeds total cost over a lifetime, but depends on course choice and individual circumstances.
